findings.summary: Gigi's generated buffer workload exposed unsupported explicit numeric-to-bool and bool-to-numeric WGSL conversions. Doe now validates and emits those conversions, and Buffers/buffertest_webgpu passes the unchanged upstream oracle.

The unchanged ReadbackSequence case exposed lost recorded texture bindings, encode-time Vulkan readback, stale JavaScript texture shadows, and a texture-copy bridge ABI mismatch. The focused case now passes under both providers and each Doe defect has a checked-in regression record.

In the second 50-case matrix, Doe passes every buffer or compute case that Dawn passes: Buffers/StructuredBuffer, Buffers/buffertest_webgpu, Compute/BufferAtomics, and Compute/ReadbackSequence. Both also pass Textures/TextureFormats.

The complete matrix is not reliable or equivalent: Dawn passes 9 of 50 cases without crashes, while Doe passes 5 of 50 and crashes in four cases. Four cases pass under Dawn but not Doe, including one crashing texture-mip case.
The host lists /dev/dri/renderD128 but denies access, so neither provider is hardware-eligible and no speed or receipt-overhead comparison was measured.

limitations: The host denied access to its physical render node, so the run cannot support a hardware performance claim.
The 50 clean processes execute distinct generated cases once; they do not provide repeated cold and warm samples for any single workload.
The run captures provider and adapter identity but not the required driver identity, shader hashes, dispatch shape, synchronization identity, readback identity, or receipt overhead.
Many cases fail under both providers because of missing assets or exact gold-image differences; those shared failures are not classified as Doe defects without a minimized comparison.
The four remaining Doe crashes and four Dawn-only passing cases prevent a complete-suite reliability or compatibility claim.

performance.reason: Each generated case ran once in a clean process on a hardware-ineligible host, so no per-workload cold/warm comparison is available.

receiptOverhead.reason: The diagnostic matrix did not execute paired receipt-disabled and receipt-enabled samples.

installation.summary: The ESM provider loader is a controlled harness substitution, not a validated production installation path.

supportHardware.summary: The physical render node was inaccessible to both provider processes.

concurrency.summary: The diagnostic matrix ran providers and cases serially.

teardown.summary: Clean-process isolation was present, but four Doe cases terminated by SIGSEGV.

stress.summary: Distinct-case breadth is not repeated stress coverage for a stable workload.

memory.summary: Peak RSS was captured, but no bounded-growth leak sequence was run.

receipts.summary: Provider and adapter identity are present, but the remaining required receipt fields and receipt overhead are absent.

performance.summary: The host is hardware-ineligible and the suite has no repeated per-case cold/warm samples.

release.summary: The harness has unresolved crashes and compatibility gaps and remains non-blocking.

ownership.summary: The I0/I1/W0/D0 ownership comparison and ownership-cost adjudication were not run.

runtimeOwnershipAssessment.summary: The retained diagnostic predates the frozen runtime-ownership comparison and cannot establish DoeRuntime attribution.
